lines: A dual acid bass synthesizer: two 16-step sequencers, each driving its own 303-style voice with a ladder filter, an envelope-modulated cutoff and a slide circuit.
Moves the edit cursor to that step of that track and plays it; in song mode it picks that phrase slot, and while the display reads LENGTH it sets that track's length to that step.
Ties the edit cursor to the running step so editing follows playback; while it is on, the copy, paste, length and transpose buttons are refused.
Chooses which track is being edited, which is the track that length, run mode, clock division, transpose and rotate apply to.
Chooses whether the panel edits one sequence of 16 steps per track, or the song's chain of phrases.
Puts the edited step's note in that octave and plays it; a tied step refuses the change and flashes a warning.
Cycles the display between transpose and rotate for the selected track, which the encoder then changes: ±24 semitones of transpose, ±16 places of rotation.
Cycles the display between length, run mode and clock division, which the encoder then changes; holding it down opens the pulses-per-step setting instead.
Changes whatever the display is showing — sequence or phrase number, track length, run mode, clock division, transpose, rotate or pulses per step; a double click returns that value to its default.
Points the keyboard at the note of the edited step, so clicking a key writes that pitch.
Points the keyboard at the gate shape of the edited step, so the twelve keys choose between twelve shapes.
Copies from the edit cursor — 4 steps, 8 steps or the whole track, as the switch beside it is set; in song mode it copies phrase slots instead.
Chooses whether CPY and PST work on 4 steps, 8 steps or the whole 16-step track.
Writes the clipboard in at the edit cursor; a copy taken in sequence mode will not paste in song mode, or the other way about.
Clears the selected track: every note and attribute, and its length, run mode, transpose, rotate and clock division; it does nothing in song mode.
Starts and stops the sequencer.
Returns both tracks to the first step.
Turns the gate of the edited step on or off.
Ties the edited step to the one before it, so the note carries through without a fresh attack.
Gives the edited step its own release time, taken from the knob beside it, instead of the release set under Expert Mode.
Sets the release time written into the edited step while that step has REL on, 21ms to 250ms.
Accents the edited step, which cuts its decay to 200ms, lifts the amplitude envelope and opens the filter further.
Cycles the edited step's condition through 1:1, 1:2, 1:4, 1st and !1st, which sets the passes on which it plays; the same five are on this button's own right-click menu.
Makes the edited step fire at random rather than every pass, at the odds set by the knob beside it.
Sets the odds that a step marked PROB fires, one figure shared by every such step in the module.
Marks the edited step to be glided into from the step before it.
Sets how long a slide takes: up to one whole step for the sequencer's CV, and up to 100ms for the two synth voices.
Chooses saw or square for that voice, and writing either one overwrites the Blend slider under Expert Mode.
Detunes that voice by up to ±700 cents, on a squared curve so small movements near the centre are fine.
Sets that voice's output level; past 75% the audio is pushed into a saturation rather than getting louder.
Sets the gain feeding that voice's filter, one to two times, which is what saturates the ladder.
Sets that voice's filter cutoff, 314Hz at the bottom of the travel to 2394Hz at the top.
Sets that voice's filter resonance; the knob is squared and scaled to 0 to 10, so the ringing arrives in the last part of the travel.
Sets how far the decay envelope opens that voice's filter above the cutoff.
Sets the decay time of that voice's filter envelope, 200ms at the bottom of the travel to 2500ms at the top.
Sets how far an accented step lifts that voice's envelope and opens its filter.
Tunes the microtuning key last clicked, ±100 cents, and that offset is applied to every note of that pitch class.
Shifts everything the sequencer plays by one octave down, nothing, or one octave up.
Sets the reference pitch, 420Hz to 460Hz, which shifts both voices; 440Hz leaves them where the CV puts them.
A trigger here starts or stops the sequencer, exactly as a press of the RUN button does.
One pulse advances the internal pulse count; the sequence moves on a step once the pulses-per-step figure is reached.
A trigger returns both tracks to the first step.
Shifts that voice's filter cutoff by 1V per octave, applied before the envelope is added.
Modulates that voice's envelope depth, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.
Modulates that voice's decay time, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.
That voice's audio, clamped at ±10V; neither voice is computed while both of these jacks are unpatched.
Note — There is no clock inside the module: nothing moves until a clock is patched and RUN is on.
Note — The wide keyboard writes the note of the edited step, or its gate shape when the GATE key mode is chosen. It is drawn as one widget, so its keys cannot be clicked for help.
Note — The dice marked RND generates a fresh acid pattern for the selected track from the settings under Randomize Track. It is not a parameter, so it cannot be clicked for help either.
Note — The dotted labels NOTE, GATE, TIE, REL, ACC, CON, PROB and SLIDE are clickable: a dimmed one keeps that attribute out of the pattern generator, so a regenerated track holds what you set.
Note — The strip reading INITIALIZE under the small keyboard steps through 47 temperaments with its two arrows, and clicking one of that keyboard's keys chooses which note the CENTS knob tunes.
Note — With TwinSlide Expander placed immediately to the right, a cable in its CV, gate, slide or fine tune input replaces the internal sequencer for that track.
Menu — Generate — under Randomize Track, writes a fresh pattern into the selected track from the settings below it
Menu — Scale — under Randomize Track, chooses which of 24 scales the generated notes are drawn from, or Random for a fresh draw each time
Menu — Density — under Randomize Track, sets how many of the steps are given a note, 0% to 100%
Menu — Spread — under Randomize Track, sets how far the generated notes are spread across octaves
Menu — Accent Density — under Randomize Track, sets how often a generated step is accented
Menu — Slide Density — under Randomize Track, sets how often a generated step is marked to slide
Menu — Transpose — under Randomize Track, shifts the generated pattern by up to ±12 semitones
Menu — Seed — under Randomize Track, 0 to 999, fixes which pattern comes out; it counts up after each generation so the next one differs
Menu — Pin Seed — under Randomize Track, stops the seed counting up, so Generate returns the same pattern
Menu — Start with Note — under Randomize Track, forces the first step of the pattern to carry a note
Menu — Start with Accent — under Randomize Track, accents the first note of the pattern
Menu — Expert Mode A — six sliders for synth A: VCF Range, Decay Speed, Sustain, Release, Blend and Bass Comp; the submenu reads 303 while all but Blend are at their defaults
Menu — Expert Mode B — the same six sliders for synth B
Menu — VCF Range — under Expert Mode, shifts the span the VCF knob covers, from 314Hz-2394Hz at the top of the slider down to 100Hz-760Hz at the bottom
Menu — Decay Speed — under Expert Mode, multiplies the rate the envelope decays at: 4 times in the middle, 6 times at the bottom of the slider and 2 times at the top
Menu — Sustain — under Expert Mode, sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate is high; 0% is the 303 behaviour and the default
Menu — Release — under Expert Mode, sets how long the envelope takes to fall once the gate ends, 21ms to 500ms
Menu — Blend — under Expert Mode, crossfades that voice between saw and square; the panel switch overwrites it
Menu — Bass Comp — under Expert Mode, moves the filter's feedback highpass between 150Hz and 500Hz, which sets how much low end the resonance cancels
Menu — Default clock resolution: x1, x4, x6, x12, x24 — sets the pulses per step a new instance and an Initialize start from; the module ships at x24, which needs a 96 PPQN clock for sixteenth notes
Menu — Reset on run — resets the sequence whenever RUN is switched on
Menu — Retrigger gates on reset: No, Yes, Only when Run cable is unconnected — sets whether a reset fires the gates of the step it lands on
Menu — Hold tied notes — holds the note through a tied step rather than cutting it
Menu — Single shot song — stops at the end of the song instead of looping
Menu — Portable sequence — copies or pastes the edited sequence in Rack's shared format, so it can be moved to another maker's sequencer; it is greyed out in song mode

TwinSlide.notes: Inputs 3 to 6 (Track A CV, Track B CV, Track A Gate, Track B Gate) and outputs 0 to 3 (Track A/B CV and gate) are configured but never given a jack on the panel; the CV and gate outputs are used internally as the bus that feeds the two voices and the expander. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), so the module is monophonic per track. Three things the manual states do not match this build: it puts the 47 temperament presets on the right-click menu, where this build has no Microtuning item at all and the presets are stepped through by the arrows beside INITIALIZE on the panel; it says a step's gate shape is chosen by holding a step button and turning the encoder, where the code takes it from the keyboard once the lower key-mode button is lit; and its Expert Mode table labels Decay Speed 6.0x as slower decay, where the figure multiplies the decay rate and so makes the envelope fall faster. The manual is written for 2.1.5 and also lists a Bass Comp scale that runs the opposite way to the code. The panel prints CPY, PST, CLR and TRANS/ROTATE where the maker's own parameter names read Copy, Paste, Clear track and Transpose / rotate; the copy button and the 4/8/T switch are both named Copy, so one of them wears the other's tooltip.

lines: A CV and gate breakout for TwinSlide, placed immediately to the right of it: the inputs replace the sequencer track by track, and the outputs carry what the sequencer is playing.
Replaces that track's pitch while a cable is in it, at 1V per octave.
Replaces that track's gate while a cable is in it; above 1V the track sounds.
Above 1V, that track glides into the note it is playing instead of stepping to it.
Detunes that track's voice, ±5V for the full ±700 cents, added to that voice's FINE knob.
Shifts the pitch of both voices by the voltage here, at 1V per octave, without touching the CV the sequencer puts out.
The pitch the sequencer is playing on that track, at 1V per octave, including its slide and microtuning.
A 10V gate while that track's step is sounding.
10V while that track is gliding between two notes, 0V otherwise.
10V while the step that track is on is marked with an accent.
Note — This module does nothing on its own: without TwinSlide immediately to its left, every output reads 0V and the inputs go nowhere.
Note — The outputs always carry the internal sequencer, even for a track whose input is being overridden, so a track can be driven from outside and read out at the same time.
Note — The mark above the input section fades from white to amber once TwinSlide is found to the left.

TwinSlideExpander.notes: Index order is not panel order: the transpose input is index 8 but sits at the top of the middle column, and the two accent outputs are indices 6 and 7 but sit in the middle column of the output section. Every port has a jack. The maker's manual describes the inputs as overriding the internal sequencer, which is what the code does, but it does not say that a slide input is read as a one-sample flag rather than a length, so a held slide gate glides every step it covers.

Sets the filter cutoff, 314Hz at the bottom of the travel to 2394Hz at the top.
Sets how far the decay envelope opens the filter above the cutoff.
Sets the decay time of the filter envelope, 200ms at the bottom of the travel to 2500ms at the top.
Chooses saw or square for the oscillator, and writing either one overwrites the Blend slider on the menu.
Sets the gain feeding the filter, one to two times, which is what saturates the ladder.
Sets how far an accent lifts the amplitude envelope and opens the filter.
Sets the filter resonance; the knob is squared and scaled to 0 to 10, so the ringing arrives in the last part of the travel.
Detunes the oscillator by up to ±700 cents, on a squared curve so small movements near the centre are fine.
Sets the output level; past 75% the audio is pushed into a saturation rather than getting louder.

Modulates the drive, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.
A gate above 1V accents the note, which cuts its decay to 200ms and lifts the envelope; the module reads this jack as a gate and not as a level, despite the panel grouping it with the CV inputs.
Detunes the oscillator, ±5V for the full ±700 cents, added to the FINE knob; the manual gives this as ±1V.
Modulates the output level, a tenth of the knob's travel per volt, added to the knob.
Sets the oscillator pitch at 1V per octave, 0V giving C4 at 261.63Hz.
A gate above 1V starts a note and holds the envelope open; the note releases when it falls.
Above 1V the pitch glides into the new note instead of stepping to it, over the time set by Slide Time on the menu.
The voice's audio, clamped at ±10V.
Note — Nothing sounds until a gate above 1V arrives at GATE; a pitch at CV on its own starts no note.
Note — The module computes nothing at all while OUT is unpatched.
Note — The display shows the name and the value of the last knob you turned.
Note — The display shows a tick against CV and against GATE while those jacks are patched, and a face instead while SLIDE is patched, with eyes that widen as the VCF knob rises.

MonoSlide.notes: Every input is read with getVoltage(), so the voice is monophonic. Two places where the manual disagrees with the code: it lists the ACC jack as accent CV, where the code compares it against 1V and uses it as a gate, the accent amount coming from the ACC knob alone; and it gives the FINE jack as ±1V for ±700 cents, where the code divides the voltage by five, so the full swing needs ±5V. The manual's MonoSlide Expert Mode table also omits Bass Comp, which is the seventh slider in the submenu, and its Decay Speed column calls 6.0x the slower setting when the figure multiplies the decay rate. Panel order and index order agree throughout.
